Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is a first-pass sizing spreadsheet and a short SKU lifecycle / fallback matrix that maps BlueMesa's two primary inference profiles to Redwood Dedicated options. High-level recommendations below so Ops/procurement can size commits: 

- Workload A (RLHF century-chat, 512–4k context, <150ms p50 soft SLO, high throughput): recommend H100-reserved slots for baseline. Rationale: best per-token throughput for FP16/AMP and supports large KV cache with minimal perf drop.
- Workload B (embeddings + batch search, variable sequence length up to 1k, throughput-oriented): recommend L4 burst instances to keep unit cost low; A100 overprovision not required.
- Memory-heavy fallback (very long context jobs / occasional fine-tuning snapshots): A100 instances are the safety net due to larger VRAM and stable perf for memory-bound cases — will be used for failure mode processing and scheduled heavy jobs.

Tradeoffs (short):
- Latency vs cost: H100 gives best latency/dollars at peak for chat; L4 is cheapest per-embedding token but cannot sustain long-context chat.
- Headroom and KV cache: H100 offers larger aggregate slot throughput; note that for 4k contexts KV cache memory per slot must be provisioned in our config.
- Preemption/failover: plan A100 fallback with 60–80% perf degradation per slot in long-context scenarios.

Ask: Can you confirm that BlueMesa prefers latency-first (primary) + cost-optimized embeddings (secondary)? If yes, I’ll push this to Ops (Irene) to formalize slot counts, canary window, and fallback thresholds.

On Mon, Dec 14, 2026 at 09:12 AM jasmine.liu@redwood.com wrote:
> Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is a first-pass sizing spreadsheet and a short SKU lifecycle / fallback matrix...

Evan — quick operational answers: 

- Perf hit explanation: 60–80% is a throughput estimate (tokens/sec) when naively swapping a tuned H100 slot for an A100 slot under the same batch/parallelism. Latency p50 can increase ~1.3–2.0x depending on seq-len distribution because A100 needs different kernel paths for some attention optimizations. We quantify this in the attached spreadsheet under the "swap-sim" tab with measured samples.

- Cold-starts on L4: L4 has smaller warm-up cost for model load (saves time) but can show higher variance on first few requests due to smaller CPU/GPU memory prefetching for large batch loads. For batch pipelines sized with a short ramp (30–90s), impact is minimal. We recommend a short, automated warm-up sequence at scale-up events (we can include in the runbook).

- 10% hedge cost delta: rough calc — moving 10% of peak chat slots from H100->A100 increases monthly committed GPU cost by ~14–18% for those slots (A100 cheaper per-slot but needs more slots to match throughput); net deal-level delta ~+4–6% depending on slot sizing. See row 42 in BlueMesa_sku_estimates_v3.xlsx.

Operational proposal (recommended):
- Commit baseline: 65% H100, 25% L4 (burst/embeddings), 10% A100 (safety/long-context).
- Canary: start with 20% of traffic on H100 slots, 80% on soft-reserve A100 fallback path for the first 2 weeks; monitor p50/p95 latency and token cost.
- Runbook: automated fallback when sustained H100 queueing > 5% for 1m, with progressive diameter (10% traffic shift per minute) until headroom recovered.

Attaching: fallback-matrix-diagram.png (ops flow), BlueMesa_sku_estimates_v3.xlsx (detailed numbers).
